citation.title: Topological dimensionality reduction-based machine learning for efficient gradient-free 3D topology optimization
citation.authors: Zhaoyou Sun; Yaguang Wang; Pai Liu; Yangjun Luo
citation.version_coded: Abstract only (OpenAlex W4283397565 / Crossref record). Full text at ScienceDirect (PII S026412752200507X, gold OA, CC BY-NC-ND) was not reachable: both the landing page (via the DOI) and the publisher's own OA PDF link (.../pdf, the same URL OpenAlex, DOAJ and Semantic Scholar all list as the open-access copy) returned HTTP 403 with an explicit Cloudflare bot challenge ('Cf-Mitigated: challenge', Server: cloudflare), checked 2026-09-24 through the fetch tool and through a direct request with a generic browser User-Agent. DOAJ's article record (e9112f3bc43446b1b351859f8aba54dc) links only back to the same sciencedirect.com URL. No arXiv id exists for this article.

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Abstract states that a material-field-series-expansion parameterization combined with a sequential neural-network surrogate reduces 3D topology-optimization design variables to under 200 and cuts computational time by 1-4 orders of magnitude compared with coarse-mesh-based gradient-free methods, while reaching design examples such as 98% of the Hashin-Shtrikman bound for bulk modulus and a 16.59% reduction in peak weld stress for a phone-dropping problem.
claim.key_phrase: reduces the computational time by 1–4 orders of magnitude compared with the coarse-mesh-based gradient-free methods
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The abstract gives only a range, '1-4 orders of magnitude' (i.e. roughly 10x to 10,000x), not a single ratio or two comparable absolute times, and does not name the specific classical comparator's identity, problem size, or hardware; picking one point value within a four-decade range would overstate precision the source does not provide, so left null rather than derived. The 98% H-S-bound and 16.59% stress-reduction figures are quality/performance results, not speed.
claim.alternatives: none stated in the abstract; abstract, conclusion, introduction and main text beyond the abstract could not be checked (full text inaccessible)

reporting.n_test_cases: not stated (abstract only; mentions 'several design problems' without a count)

notes: Full text not accessible through any legal route tried: the DOI landing page and the publisher's own gold-OA PDF link (both sciencedirect.com) returned HTTP 403 with an explicit Cloudflare bot-check header; per the access rules this challenge was not bypassed. OpenAlex, DOAJ and Semantic Scholar were all checked and each points only to the same blocked ScienceDirect location; no arXiv preprint or institutional-repository copy was found. Per the second-pass access rule, coded from the abstract as an include with reason 'I-UNCLEAR (no accessible full text)', stratum 'none', and all rule verdicts 'na', rather than excluded, even though the abstract's own '1-4 orders of magnitude' claim would otherwise suggest the speed stratum. included.physics = 'other' [inferred with low confidence] because the abstract's two headline examples span different physics categories not cleanly captured by one closed-list value: an effective bulk-modulus (metamaterial homogenization-type) result and a nonlinear-dynamic peak-weld-stress result from a phone-dropping simulation (closer to 'stress' but transient/nonlinear rather than the quasi-static stress-constrained TO the protocol describes); this should be revisited if full text becomes accessible. included.method_family = 'surrogate_mlp_gp' fits the stated 'sequential neural network surrogate model' used to explore the dimensionality-reduced design space. Duplicate check against audit/pool/pool.csv: no other pool record shares this title, DOI or a close paraphrase (only a generic Chinese-language survey record matched on an empty-string false positive from the dedup script's CJK handling, not a real duplicate).
